properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. It comes from a cost that was PAID, not predicted.

═══ THE MEASURED INSTANCE, 2026-08-25 ═══

`unreviewed_ideas` fired correctly on 2026-08-23 with "110 of 181 open idea(s) connect to nothing", and Anthony accepted it: *"A parked idea legitimately governs nothing yet, and relating them on a guess would assert reasoning nobody did."* THAT REASONING IS CORRECT and matches the detector's own warning that a false neighbour is worse than a missing one.

🛑 BUT THE FINDING IS AGGREGATE-KEYED, so one acceptance silenced it PERMANENTLY — for every idea written since and every idea that will ever be written. Two days later, on 2026-08-25, the cost landed exactly where the gap predicted: a session reasoning about functional allocation never reached `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph`, which had ANTICIPATED that session's central error seventeen days earlier and said so in as many words. **The user had to be the index.** He named it himself: *"these brainstorming ideas from the past should slowly be being linked together, so that next time we have a discussion on functional allocation, I don't have to remind you."*

Measured the same day: 174 idea nodes, **121 of them (70%) link to no other idea at all**; only 43 idea-to-idea edges exist across the whole set.

═══ WHY THE PENDULUM IS THE POINT ═══

`is_aggregate` EXISTS because the opposite failed: `unvalidated_capability` was re-acknowledged about twenty times — at 33, 34, 35 … 68 capabilities — always with the same disposition, because per-node keying expired the judgement on every write. That was a real defect and aggregate keying was a real fix.

⭐ SO THE TWO KNOWN STATES ARE "EXPIRES ON EVERY WRITE" AND "NEVER EXPIRES", and both have now cost something. The unexplored middle is an acceptance that carries the POPULATION IT WAS ACCEPTED AT and re-asks when that moves materially — accepted at 110 of 181, asked again at 150 of 220. Nobody has to re-judge an unchanged situation, and nobody silently inherits a judgement made about a much smaller one.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**A. POPULATION-DRIFT EXPIRY.** The acknowledgement records the numerator/denominator at acceptance; the gap re-fires past a threshold. Fixes all five aggregate kinds at the root.
 ⚠️ Cost: it re-opens existing acknowledgements across `unreviewed_ideas`, `undeclared_seam`, `change_axis_unstated`, `unvalidated_capability` and `no_published_boundary` at once. Threshold choice is a new knob, and a badly chosen one recreates the flood.

**B. LEAVE IT, AND TREAT THE BACKLOG AS THE ANSWER.** The gap is honest; the fix is to work the 110 down with `review_relations` rather than to change the mechanism.
 ⚠️ Cost: says nothing about the NEXT aggregate acceptance, and the same trap is available to every aggregate gap including `unallocated_component`, added the same day.

**C. PER-KIND CHOICE.** Some aggregates are about a PRACTICE that does not change with scale ("we publish nothing on purpose"); others are about a BACKLOG whose size is the whole point. Only the second kind expires.
 ⭐ This is the sharpest reading — `no_published_boundary` genuinely should never expire, and `unreviewed_ideas` genuinely should. It needs a per-variant judgement rather than one rule.

📌 DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO WORK LANDING TODAY: `unallocated_component` (PR #336) is aggregate-keyed on the same anti-flood argument, and is a BACKLOG-shaped finding — 33 of 85 leaf components on reflow2's own design. Under option C it is exactly the kind that should expire. It shipped before this was noticed, which is why this node exists rather than a quiet edit.
properties.name: OPEN — an aggregate gap accepted once stays accepted forever, however much the population grows. Should the acceptance expire when the population moves materially?
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the reasoning survives without being claimed as intent, and LINKED on creation rather than left to a later sweep — which is the discipline this node is about. Anthony, 2026-08-25, on the half-ideas: they should be linked as they are written so a later discussion finds the line of reasoning instead of an orphan.

Kept as an open idea rather than filed as a defect because the mechanism is not wrong — aggregate keying fixed a real and worse problem, and both known settings have now cost something. What is missing is the middle, and choosing it is a judgement about each variant rather than a bug fix.
